originality.rationale: Qualitative selection bias and the benefit of independent requerying are explicitly prior insights, especially in Shvaiko and Rebrova (2026). The additional claim is the explicit Rademacher scalar exact finite-sample risk for two-stage sampled-with-replacement updates, a screening-fraction half-threshold for positive asymptotic error, and an exponentially long sign-dwell law for the all-eligible-row cached update. The precise antecedents examined do not imply these exact statements under their hypotheses. This is a qualified best-knowledge novelty assessment; a simpler previously published equivalent calculation remains possible.

The strict positive q<1 floor and exponentially long sign persistence despite symmetric fresh noise are independently interpretable stress tests and sharpen the prior qualitative selection-bias warning. No general matrix significance or computational superiority is asserted.
